sec: Pulmonary renal syndrome & Goodpasture HLA · p781

items.q: Pulmonary renal syndrome is defined as:
opts: RPGN (kidney involvement) plus diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (lung involvement)
Nephrotic syndrome plus pulmonary embolism with pulmonary infarction
Acute kidney injury plus cardiogenic pulmonary oedema with pleural effusion
Chronic kidney disease plus obstructive sleep apnoea with nocturnal hypoxaemia
items.exp: Pulmonary renal syndrome = RPGN (kidney involvement) + diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (lung involvement). (Book p781)

items.q: All of the following are listed conditions under pulmonary renal syndrome EXCEPT:
items.exp: Conditions listed: Goodpasture syndrome, microscopic polyangiitis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis and SLE (active disease). PSGN is not listed here. (Book p781)

items.q: Active SLE is listed as one of the conditions causing pulmonary renal syndrome.
opts: False — SLE causes only nephrotic syndrome
True, but only in drug-induced lupus
False — SLE is excluded because C3 is normal
items.exp: The conditions list for pulmonary renal syndrome ends with SLE (active disease). (Book p781)

items.q: According to the note, RPGN with diffuse alveolar haemorrhage and a non-specific antibody is:
opts: SLE with class V lupus nephritis
items.exp: Note: RPGN + DAH + antibody (non-specific) = anti-GBM disease; the antibody in question is anti-GBM. (Book p781)

items.q: Fill up: Goodpasture disease is RPGN + diffuse alveolar haemorrhage + antibody against the noncollagenous domain of the ______ chain of type-IV collagen.
items.exp: Goodpasture disease = RPGN + DAH + antibody against the noncollagenous domain of the α3 chain of type-IV collagen. (Book p781)

items.q: Fill up: Besides smoking, hydrocarbon exposure and lung infection, the fourth 2nd/trigger factor listed for Goodpasture disease is ______.
items.exp: 2nd/trigger factors for Goodpasture disease: smoking, hydrocarbon exposure, fluid overload and lung infection. (Book p781)

items.q: Which is NOT a listed trigger for Goodpasture disease?
items.exp: Listed triggers: smoking, hydrocarbon exposure, fluid overload and lung infection. A streptococcal sore throat relates to PSGN, not Goodpasture disease. (Book p781)

items.q: Which HLA pair carries the highest risk in Goodpasture disease?
items.exp: HLA association in Goodpasture disease: high risk DR2/15 and DR4; low risk DR1 and DR7. (Book p781)

items.q: A 25-year-old heavy smoker has haemoptysis, a fall in Hb and rapidly rising creatinine; anti-GBM antibody is positive. Which HLA type would be expected to increase his risk?
items.exp: High-risk HLA types in Goodpasture disease are DR2/15 and DR4; DR1 and DR7 are low risk. (Book p781)

items.q: Which HLA type is protective/low-risk in Goodpasture disease rather than high-risk?
items.exp: Low-risk HLA types: DR1 and DR7. High risk: DR2/15 and DR4. (Book p781)
